10374-the-ramblin-kid.title: The Ramblin Kid
10374-the-ramblin-kid.creator: Unknown
10374-the-ramblin-kid.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The other, known on the Kiowa and the range of western Texas and Mexico only as "the Ramblin' Kid," strolled leisurely out through the sagging, weight-swung gate and up to the panting horse from which Skinny had not yet dismounted.

arxiv-1910-01781.title: Distributionally Robust XVA via Wasserstein Distance: Wrong Way Counterparty Credit and Funding Risk
arxiv-1910-01781.creator: Derek Singh, Shuzhong Zhang
arxiv-1910-01781.description: Abstract This paper investigates calculations of robust XVA, in particular, credit valuation adjustment (CVA) and funding valuation adjustment (FVA) for over-the-counter derivatives under distributional uncertainty using Wasserstein distance as the ambiguity measure. Wrong way counterparty credit risk and funding risk can be characterized (and indeed quantified) via the robust XVA formulations.

arxiv-2108-06294.title: Ghosts without runaway Preprint: YITP-21-82, IPMU21-0052
arxiv-2108-06294.creator: Cédric Deffayet, Shinji Mukohyama, Alexander Vikman
arxiv-2108-06294.description: Abstract We present a simple class of mechanical models where a canonical degree of freedom interacts with another one with a negative kinetic term, i.e. with a ghost. We prove analytically that the classical motion of the system is completely stable for all initial conditions, notwithstanding that the conserved Hamiltonian is unbounded from below and above.

arxiv-2205-00496.title: Explicit spacetime-symmetry breaking and the dynamics of primordial fields
arxiv-2205-00496.creator: Nils A. Nilsson
arxiv-2205-00496.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Nils A. Nilsson. We study the effects of explicit spacetime-symmetry breaking on primordial tensor fluctuations using an effective-field theory for Lorentz/CPT violation. We find that the graviton is still massless, but that the propagation speed of tensor modes is modified, and we obtain a constraint on the coefficient determining the symmetry breaking on the order of 10 − 15 10^{-15} from the recent measurements of the speed of gravity.

arxiv-2209-02353.title: From Legal Contracts to Legal Calculi: the code-driven normativity
arxiv-2209-02353.creator: Silvia Crafa
arxiv-2209-02353.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Silvia Crafa. Using dedicated software to represent or enact legislation or regulation has the advantage of solving the inherent ambiguity of legal texts and enabling the automation of compliance with legal norms. On the other hand, the so-called code-driven normativity is less flexible than the legal provisions it claims to implement, and transforms the nature of legal protection, potentially reducing the capability of individual human beings to invoke legal remedies.

arxiv-2212-05910.title: Self-dual matroids from canonical curves
arxiv-2212-05910.creator: Alheydis Geiger, Sachi Hashimoto, Bernd Sturmfels and Raluca Vlad
arxiv-2212-05910.description: Abstract Self-dual configurations of 2 ​ n 2n points in a projective space of dimension n − 1 n-1 were studied by Coble, Dolgachev–Ortland, and Eisenbud–Popescu. We examine the self-dual matroids and self-dual valuated matroids defined by such configurations, with a focus on those arising from hyperplane sections of canonical curves.

arxiv-2301-00509.creator: Antoine Djogbenou,
arxiv-2301-00509.description: Abstract 1 Introduction The total market capitalization of cryptocurrencies is currently over 1 trillion U.S. dollar, with the top three cryptocurrencies in terms of market capitalization being Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and Tether (USDT). While Bitcoin and Euthereum are characterized by high price volatility, Tether is a stablecoin, i.e.

arxiv-2305-06824.title: Genesis of chimera patterns through self-induced stochastic resonance
arxiv-2305-06824.creator: Taniya Khatun, Tanmoy Banerjee
arxiv-2305-06824.description: Abstract Noise induced order in excitable systems has diverse manifestations, such as coherence resonance (CR) and stochastic resonance. In this context a less explored phenomenon is self-induced stochastic resonance (SISR). Unlike CR, SISR may arise away from the bifurcation threshold and the properties of the induced oscillations depend upon both the noise intensity and the time-scale separation factor.

arxiv-2307-11930.title: Highly-mass-loaded hot galactic winds are unstable to cool filament formation 2023 Highly-mass-loaded hot galactic winds are unstable to cool filament formation – B
arxiv-2307-11930.creator: Dustin D. Nguyen, Todd A. Thompson, Evan E. Schneider, & Ashley P. Tarrant
arxiv-2307-11930.description: Abstract When cool clouds are ram-pressure accelerated by a hot supersonic galactic wind, some of the clouds may be shredded by hydrodynamical instabilities and incorporated into the hot flow. Recent one-dimensional steady-state calculations show how cool cloud entrainment directly affects the bulk thermodynamics, kinematics, and observational characteristics of the hot gas.

arxiv-2310-14366.title: Bi-Encoders based Species Normalization - Pairwise Sentence Learning to Rank
arxiv-2310-14366.creator: ZZainab Awan, TKTim Kahlke, PJ RPeter J. Ralph, PJ KPaul J. Kennedy
arxiv-2310-14366.description: Abstract \parttitle Motivation Biomedical named-entity normalization involves connecting biomedical entities with distinct database identifiers in order to facilitate data integration across various fields of biology. Existing systems for biomedical named entity normalization heavily rely on dictionaries, manually created rules, and high-quality representative features such as lexical or morphological characteristics.

arxiv-2408-04925.title: Spherically symmetric loop quantum gravity: Schwarzschild spacetimes with a cosmological constant
arxiv-2408-04925.creator: Esteban Mato 1, Javier Olmedo 2, Sahil Saini 3
arxiv-2408-04925.description: Abstract We provide a quantization of the Schwarzschild spacetime in the presence of a cosmological constant, based on midisuperspace methods developed in the spherically symmetric sector of loop quantum gravity, using in particular the ’improved dynamics’ scheme. We include both the de Sitter and anti-de Sitter cases.

arxiv-2512-02718.title: Irreduciblity of certain 𝔰 ​ l ^ 2 \widehat{\mathfrak{s}l}_{2} –modules of Wakimoto type
arxiv-2512-02718.creator: Dražen Adamović, Veronika Pedić Tomić
arxiv-2512-02718.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Dražen Adamović, Veronika Pedić Tomić. We investigate the irreducible smooth 𝔰 ​ 𝔩 ^ 2 \widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_{2} –modules recently constructed in [ 13 ] , and demonstrate that these modules admit a Wakimoto-type realization at both critical and non-critical levels. In the critical level case, we identify simple quotients of these modules with the Wakimoto modules whose irreducibility was already established in [ 1 , 2 ] .

arxiv-2601-07776.title: On wall-crossing coordinates in Cerf theory
arxiv-2601-07776.creator: Roger Casals
arxiv-2601-07776.description: Abstract . We relate Bruhat numbers in real Morse theory to cluster variables in braid varieties. This provides instances of wall-crossing coordinates in the study of Cerf diagrams. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary: 53D10. Secondary: 57K43, 13F60. 1. Introduction The object of this short note is to relate Bruhat numbers in real Morse theory to cluster variables in braid varieties.

arxiv-2602-23786.title: The origin of complex behavior of liquid carbon: an insight from computer simulation
arxiv-2602-23786.creator: Yu. D. Fomin
arxiv-2602-23786.description: Abstract In the present paper we perfomrm molecular dynamics simulation of liquid carbon with a machine-learning potential GAP-20. We show that within the framework of this model carbon demonstrates a relatively low critical temperature, which can affect the results of experimental measurements of melting point of graphite. Keywords :speed of sound, binary mixture, phase diagram, Frenkel line pacs 61.20.Gy, 61.20.

europmc-pmc3316511.title: Impact of multi-targeted antiretroviral treatment on gut T cell depletion and HIV reservoir seeding during acute HIV infection.
europmc-pmc3316511.creator: Ananworanich J, Schuetz A, Vandergeeten C, Sereti I, de Souza M, Rerknimitr R, Dewar R, Marovich M, van Griensven F, Sekaly R, Pinyakorn S, Phanuphak N, Trichavaroj R, Rutvisuttinunt W, Chomchey N, Paris R, Peel S, Valcour V, Maldarelli F, Chomont N, Michael N, Phanuphak P, Kim JH, RV254/SEARCH 010 Study Group.

This study aims to characterize the earliest immunologic and virologic HIV events following infection and investigates the usage of a novel therapeutic strategy. Method

pmc-10694953.title: Mildly elevated serum bilirubin and its correlations with lipid levels among male patients undergoing health checkups
pmc-10694953.creator: Xin Bai, Jing Qiao, Hong Zhang
pmc-10694953.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundBilirubin’s ability to lower lipid levels was confirmed by several studies, but those studies mainly focused on total bilirubin (TBil). The present study aimed to elucidate the correlations of the two subtypes of bilirubin with lipid levels.MethodsA total of 1732 male patients undergoing health checkups were categorized into three groups according to the levels of direct bilirubin (DBil) and indirect bilirubin (IBil).

pmc-11418110.title: Biosynthetic mechanisms of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids in microalgae
pmc-11418110.creator: Kaiwen Sun, Dauenpen Meesapyodsuk, Xiao Qiu
pmc-11418110.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Marine microalgae are the primary producers of ω3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), such as octadecapentaenoic acid (OPA, 18:5n-3) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA, 22:6n-3) for food chains. However, the biosynthetic mechanisms of these PUFAs in the algae remain elusive. To study how these fatty acids are synthesized in microalgae, a series of radiolabeled precursors were used to trace the biosynthetic process of PUFAs in Emiliania huxleyi.

pmc-11600214.title: Exploring Protein Conformational Changes Using a Large‐Scale Biophysical Sampling Augmented Deep Learning Strategy
pmc-11600214.creator: Yao Hu, Hao Yang, Mingwei Li, Zhicheng Zhong, Yongqi Zhou, Fang Bai, Qian Wang
pmc-11600214.description: Inspired by the success of deep learning in predicting static protein structures, researchers are now actively exploring other deep learning algorithms aimed at predicting the conformational changes of proteins. Currently, a major challenge in the development of such models lies in the limited training data characterizing different conformational transitions.

pmc-11652293.title: Biomechanical Comparison of Surgical Steel Wiring and Suture Tape Tension Band Techniques for Arthrodesis of the Metacarpophalangeal and Proximal Interphalangeal Joint
pmc-11652293.creator: Michael J McKernan, Miguel A Diaz, Michael Kucharik, Nino Coutelle, Peter Simon, Michael C Doarn
pmc-11652293.description: PurposeThe purpose of this study was to evaluate the biomechanical properties of SutureTape as an alternative technique for arthrodesis of the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) and proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint arthrodesis when compared with surgical steel wire.MethodsA total of 32 fingers (index, long, ring, and small) from two matched pair cadaveric hands were used.

pmc-12502632.title: Superficial fungal infections in children in Northern Finland between 2000 and 2021: a single-center study
pmc-12502632.creator: Kiia Korpi, Eetu Kiviniemi, Jari Jokelainen, Laura Huilaja, Suvi-Päivikki Sinikumpu
pmc-12502632.description: Superficial fungal infections in children are less prevalent compared with adults, and there are limited data on epidemiology in Northern Europe. This study retrospectively observed the epidemiological factors and treatment patterns of these infections in children in Northern Finland between 2000 and 2021.

pmc-12510572.title: Isolation, identification and antibacterial activity of endophytes from the seeds of Panax japonicus
pmc-12510572.creator: Rui Jin, Tingting Tang, Xilun Huang, Juan Huang, E. Liang, Lai Zhang, Abhay Pandey, Raed Haleem, Raed Haleem, Raed Haleem
pmc-12510572.description: The purpose of this study is to isolate and identify endophytes from the seeds of Panax japonicus, find growth-promoting endophyte that favors seed germination in P. japonicus, and provide theoretical reference for further research on the effect of endophytes on seed germination.MethodsThe streak plate method isolated the endophytic bacteria from the seeds.

pmc-12542531.title: Trends and factors associated with modern contraceptive use among sexually active female youths in Tanzania, 2004–2022
pmc-12542531.creator: Farida Ollomy, Sia E Msuya, Jim Todd, Sylvia Meku, Ednah Loishiye Samwel, Jackson Lutobeka, Erick A Mboya, Douglas Ndeki, Innocent B Mboya
pmc-12542531.description: ObjectiveThe study aimed to assess the trends and factors associated with modern contraceptive use among female youths (15–24 years) in Tanzania from 2004 to 2022.DesignWe performed secondary analysis of cross-sectional data from four consecutive Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) in Tanzania: 2004, 2010, 2015/2016 and 2022.SettingTanzania.ParticipantsSexually active female youths (n=8659).

pmc-12967574.title: SLC12A8 Drives Immune Evasion and Metastasis in Luminal B Breast Cancer by Inducing CD8 + T‐Cell Exhaustion via the TLR Signaling Pathway
pmc-12967574.creator: Zhiyong Liu, Ran Chen
pmc-12967574.description: BackgroundTo investigate the role and mechanism of SLC12A8 in the progression of Luminal B breast cancer.MethodsData from TCGA, GTEx, and HPA databases were used to analyze SLC12A8 expression and its prognostic value in breast cancer. qPCR was performed to validate SLC12A8 expression in various breast cancer cell lines.

pmc-13156632.title: Comparative evaluation of antioxidant, cytoprotective, and anti-arthritic activities of pomegranate peel powder and coarse powdered date seeds: implications for functional nutrition
pmc-13156632.creator: Madyha H Mahmoud, Abdulrahman A Alsayegh, Nahla Kambal, Asrar Alsaeedi, Boshra M Mozaffar, Eman Merghani A Mohammed, Ashwag H Alwadani, Halah Abdulrahman Hafiz
pmc-13156632.description: Highlights•Pomegranate peel powder (PPP) showed significantly stronger antioxidant activity than coarse powdered date seeds across all assays.•PPP provided superior cytoprotective effects through erythrocyte membrane stabilization and protection against oxidative DNA damage.•Anti-arthritic potential of PPP was confirmed by marked inhibition of protein denaturation and protease activity.•The biological efficacy of PPP is attributed to synergistic multi-target interactions of its polyphenolic constituents.

pmc-13281505.title: Individual, interpersonal, organizational, and community contexts: factors associated with alcohol consumption among Brazilian adolescents
pmc-13281505.creator: Lidiane Moura Coelho, Mery Natali Silva Abreu, Erika Gisseth Leon Ramirez, Laura de Souza Cury, Alanna Gomes da Silva
pmc-13281505.description: BackgroundAdolescence is a development period characterized by biological, psychological, and social changes that may lead to risk behaviors, such as alcohol consumption. Family, school, and community contexts, together with exposure to different communication media, may contribute to adolescents’ vulnerability to alcohol use.ObjectiveTo identify individual, interpersonal-, organizational-, and community-level factors associated with current alcohol consumption among Brazilian adolescents.

pmc-13378256.title: Butyrate causes loss of specific acetylation by the histone acetyltransferase p300
pmc-13378256.creator: Muwei Jiang, Anthi Psoma, Jinxiao Lyu, Maria Gabriella Chiariello, Rutger Modderman, Frans Bianchi, Danny Incarnato, Siewert-Jan Marrink, Iris H Jonkers, Geert van den Bogaart
pmc-13378256.description: SummaryButyrate, a short-chain fatty acid produced by microbial fermentation of dietary fiber, exerts beneficial metabolic and immunomodulatory functions through butyrylation of the histone acetyltransferase p300. This is thought to result in histone hyperacetylation at transcription starting sites and enhancers that regulate specific genes. However, we show that butyrate-induced hyperacetylation is not specific but occurs at histones throughout the entire genome.

pmc-13391943.title: Not just Rubisco: integrated strategies to overcome the biochemical limitations of C3 photosynthesis
pmc-13391943.creator: Shivasharanappa S. Patil, Bagyalakshmi Muthan, Sanju A. Sanjaya
pmc-13391943.description: Photosynthesis is fundamental to global food security, but carbon assimilation efficiency in most C3 crops remains significantly below its theoretical maximum. Three principal biochemical processes limit photosynthetic performance: ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (Rubisco) catalytic activity, ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP) regeneration via the Calvin-Benson-Bassham (CBB) cycle, and triose-phosphate utilization (TPU) for sucrose and starch biosynthesis.

pmc-13654037.title: Survival after lymph node dissection, radiotherapy, and combined treatment in sentinel node–positive stage IIIA Merkel cell carcinoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13654037.creator: Sophia Wasserer, Yannick Foerster, Sarah Preis, Felix Lauffer, Tilo Biedermann, Oana-Diana Persa, Kristine Elisabeth Mayer
pmc-13654037.description: BackgroundMerkel cell carcinoma (MCC) has a high risk of regional lymphatic metastasis. In cases of lymphatic micrometastasis, an evidence-based clinical approach is missing.ObjectiveTo assess survival outcomes following complete lymph node dissection (CLND), radiation (RTX), or CLND plus RTX (CLND + RTX) in patients with stage IIIA MCC.MethodsA systematic search was conducted in MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library.

pmc-13672684.title: Atlas‐Guided CD55‐Enriched Neutrophil Extracellular Vesicles for Complement–Macrophage Modulation in Diabetic Wounds
pmc-13672684.creator: Tairong Cui, Jieying Li, Jibing He, Jia Wang, Yun Qian, Yilin Jin, Liuqing Yang, Zaijin Tao, Ziyun Li, Zhengsheng Chen, Wenjing Wang, Xin Ma, Jinglei Wu
pmc-13672684.description: Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation and impaired immune resolution, yet the therapeutic translation of single‐cell atlases into rational immunomodulatory strategies remains limited. Here, integration of diabetic‐wound single‐cell transcriptomic datasets identifies a neutrophil subpopulation enriched in cluster of differentiation 55 (CD55) with complement‐regulatory and reparative features.
